findings.issue_text: [BUG] The deleteMany OR-clause deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method, so non-SMS reminders and not-yet-scheduled reminders with two failures are permanently destroyed instead of retried. A reminder whose Twilio call failed twice (catch path increments retryCount) is deleted by the next run of this handler before it can ever be scheduled — the workflow reminder is silently dropped and the attendee never gets it; the same clause also matches reminders of other methods since the OR bypasses the method: SMS filter.

[BUG] The catch-block prisma.workflowReminder.update throws an unhandled P2025 rejection when the reminder row was already deleted by the deleteMany at the top of a concurrent run (retryCount > 1), masking the original error and crashing the request. During overlapping invocations of this endpoint (cron overlap), the second update on a deleted row rejects, the catch block itself throws, and the loop aborts leaving remaining reminders unscheduled for that pass.

[ADVISORY] The cast to (PartialWorkflowReminder & { retryCount: number })[] hand-augments the Prisma-generated select type instead of relying on Prisma's inferred select return type, duplicating the field definition that schema.prisma already declares. The next contributor who adds a field to the select must update this hand-maintained intersection type in parallel; a drift between the cast and the actual select silently produces undefined at runtime while TypeScript believes it is a number.

[BUG] The retryCount-based deleteMany branch drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so the purge matches any WorkflowReminder of any method whose retryCount exceeds 1. The OR branch "{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }" carries no method or scheduledDate constraint, so any workflow reminder (e.g., an SMS one is the only current writer, but the query itself is method-agnostic) with retryCount > 1 is hard-deleted even when its scheduledDate is in the future — and any future writer that sets retryCount on EMAIL/other-method reminders will have those reminders silently deleted by the SMS scheduling cron. Even today, a reminder that fails twice is deleted regardless of date, which is the cap working, but the missing method filter is the sibling condition on the same query that the original code carefully enforced.

[ADVISORY] Retry-limit behavior (retryCount starting at 0, incremented on failure, purge at > 1) is implemented with no test or verification anywhere in the diff. Scanning the diff for test-shaped files (spec/**, test/**, *.test.*, *.spec.*) finds none; the new state machine (0 -> 1 -> deleted) is entirely untested, so an off-by-one in the purge threshold (gt 1 vs gte 1, or default 0 vs 1) would silently change reminder lifetime and no CI signal would catch it. Operators relying on 'one retry then drop' have no acceptance criterion documented or verified.

[ADVISORY] retryCount is incremented with a non-atomic read-then-write (reminder.retryCount + 1 from the pre-loop query), not prisma's atomic { increment: 1 }. The value is read once before the per-reminder loop and written back as retryCount + 1; if any other concurrent process (the cron running on a second instance, or a retry of this handler) updates the same reminder between the findMany and the update, increments are lost and a flaky reminder is retried more times than the intended cap. Using { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } removes the race and makes the update idempotent against concurrent schedulers.

[ADVISORY] The new else branch and the catch branch duplicate identical retryCount-increment update blocks instead of a shared increment. The two prisma.workflowReminder.update calls are byte-identical; the next change to retry policy (e.g., adding a lastRetryAt or capping at a constant) must be edited in two places and will drift, which is exactly how the sibling-flag/parallel-logic class of bug appears. A single incrementRetryCount(reminder.id) helper would delete one block.

[BUG] The retryCount>1 deletion branch of the deleteMany OR clause omits the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so any WorkflowReminder of any method with retryCount > 1 is destroyed by this SMS-scheduling handler. WorkflowReminder is a shared table used by email and other reminder methods; the moment any other code path (or a future backport) writes retryCount on a non-SMS reminder, this endpoint silently deletes those email reminders, cancelling reminders for bookings with no trace. The PR's stated scope is SMS retry tracking, but the deletion predicate now reaches beyond SMS.

[ADVISORY] Both retry-increment sites (the no-phone-number else branch and the catch block) use the stale in-memory reminder.retryCount + 1 rather than an atomic increment, and both fire unconditionally on any error. Concurrent cron invocations of this handler (or two app instances) read the same retryCount and both write the same incremented value, so a reminder that failed N times records fewer retries and lingers longer than the 2-retry cap implies; non-retryable errors (invalid template, auth failure) also burn retries identically to transient Twilio errors. Bitten by: operators expecting bounded retry semantics.

[ADVISORY] The retryCount>1 deletion predicate is evaluated only inside this handler's cron run and removes retried reminders entirely rather than marking them failed, so no failure state is ever observable. A booking whose SMS reminder permanently fails twice has its reminder row hard-deleted; admins investigating 'why did the guest not get the SMS' find no record the reminder ever existed or failed, since the only trace is a console.log. Who gets bitten: support/debugging after the fact.

[BUG] The retryCount>1 branch of deleteMany drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS constraint, so the delete condition matches WorkflowReminder rows of ANY method once retryCount exceeds 1. The predicate is no longer scoped to SMS: any future writer that sets retryCount on an email (or other-method) reminder — or a shared retry helper — causes this SMS cron to permanently delete those rows, silently cancelling email reminders for bookings. Even today it makes the delete semantics dependent on the implicit invariant that only this file writes retryCount, an invariant nothing in the schema enforces.

[ADVISORY] Rows that failed SMS scheduling twice are hard-deleted (retryCount > 1) with no audit trail, logging, or soft-delete marker. Bookings silently lose their SMS reminders after two transient Twilio errors (rate limit, network blip); neither the operator nor the booker has any record the reminder existed and failed — the `referenceId`/error string in the catch is only console-logged, and the row carrying it is then destroyed. Ops gets no signal that a booking lost a reminder.

[ADVISORY] retryCount is incremented via read-modify-write (reminder.retryCount + 1 from the in-memory row fetched at query time) rather than an atomic { increment: 1 } update. If the cron runs concurrently (overlapping scheduler invocations on the same instance or multiple instances), both read retryCount=1 and both write 2, so a reminder that actually failed four times is counted as two and survives two extra retry cycles; the retry cap is enforced only approximately under concurrency.

[ADVISORY] The catch block increments retryCount for every error class, including non-retryable ones, and the schedule attempt for that reminder is abandoned for this run with no distinction between transient and permanent failures. A permanent failure (e.g. invalid phone number rejected by Twilio) still consumes both retries and then the row is deleted, masking a configuration problem as normal retry-cap exhaustion; an operator debugging why a booking got no SMS finds only a generic console.log, not a persisted failure reason.

[BUG] The deleteMany OR branch matching retryCount > 1 has no method filter, so reminders for any delivery method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP_APP, etc.) that have hit the retry threshold are deleted by the SMS scheduling endpoint, not just SMS ones. When the SMS cron endpoint runs, any non-SMS WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 is hard-deleted; those reminders silently vanish with no send attempt and no audit, and since nothing else in the codebase writes retryCount yet, future failed email retries will be destroyed by an unrelated SMS job. If SMS retries are the intent, the retryCount branch must also constrain method: WorkflowMethods.SMS.

[BUG] The catch block increments retryCount without distinguishing transient errors (Twilio rate limit) from permanent failures (invalid phone number, malformed booking payload), so permanently-failing reminders are retried exactly twice and then silently deleted by the sweeper. Every unremovable bad phone number produces two wasted Twilio API calls and two DB writes per reminder, then the reminder is deleted with only a console.log as record — the organizer/attendee is never told the reminder was permanently dropped, and there is no way to distinguish 'never attempted' from 'attempted and failed 2x' once the row is deleted.

[BUG] The new OR branch in the deleteMany where clause drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so any reminder of any method with retryCount > 1 is deleted, not just SMS reminders. Email or other non-SMS workflow reminders whose retryCount exceeds 1 are hard-deleted by this handler, permanently destroying scheduled reminders for bookings before they fire — silent data loss with no recovery path (deleteMany is not soft-delete).

[ADVISORY] The retryCount increment uses a non-atomic read-then-write (reminder.retryCount + 1) inside a loop over stale in-memory data, and the catch-block update runs against a reminder that may have been deleted earlier in the same run. Concurrent executions of this scheduler (overlapping cron invocations) undercount retries, so failed SMS reminders are retried indefinitely — the retry cap the change exists to enforce is bypassed; the catch-path update on a deleted id throws P2025, aborting the remaining loop iterations so later reminders are never scheduled.

[BUG] The new `OR: [{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` branch in the deleteMany destroys failed reminders instead of just unscheduling them, deleting rows whose scheduledDate is still in the future. Any SMS reminder that failed to schedule twice (retryCount reaches 2) is permanently deleted from WorkflowReminder even though its scheduledDate is in the future — the booking's step loses its reminder record entirely (no cancelled flag, no audit trail), and the attendee silently never gets the SMS; this is unconditional destructive DELETE with no backup/export path, and the loss is silent because the loop below simply finds nothing to schedule.

[BUG] retryCount is never reset to 0 on successful scheduling, so transient failures accumulate across independent scheduling cycles. A reminder that failed once months ago (retryCount=1), was scheduled successfully on the next run, and then hits a single new Twilio failure is deleted at retryCount=2 — the counter measures lifetime failures, not consecutive retries, so a single transient outage permanently destroys the reminder that the retry-count design intended to allow.

[ADVISORY] The catch-block increments retryCount via `where: { id: reminder.id }` with no guard for the record having been concurrently deleted (e.g., by the deleteMany in a parallel pod or a booking cancellation) or for the update itself failing. When the row is gone between fetch and update, Prisma throws P2025 out of the catch block, the handler returns a 500, and the remaining reminders in the loop are never processed — one dead record wedges the whole scheduling pass.

[BUG] The new `OR: [{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` branch of the deleteMany permanently deletes reminders that failed to schedule twice, even when their scheduledDate is still in the future, with no log, no error, and no user-visible signal. A reminder whose Twilio send failed twice (e.g., transient provider outage) is silently dropped from the database on the next cron invocation; the API still returns `{ ok: true }` and the booking recipient never receives the reminder and no one is told — silent partial success / dropped work.

[BUG] Both the else-branch and the catch block increment retryCount with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` computed from the value read before the loop's awaits, instead of an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`, so concurrent invocations of the endpoint interleave and lost updates occur. If this handler runs concurrently (overlapping cron runs or a manual trigger racing the cron), two workers read the same retryCount, each write `read+1`, and one failure is counted once instead of twice — the reminder's retry budget is silently over-extended (or the deleteMany cleanup never triggers), leaving stale unscheduled reminders that neither send nor get cleaned up.

[BUG] The catch block increments retryCount unconditionally, including when the thrown error occurs after a successful send/scheduling update already executed earlier in the try body for the same or prior reminder, double-counting retries against a reminder that was actually scheduled. An exception thrown later in the try body (e.g., by a subsequent await or Prisma update failure) causes retryCount to be incremented on a reminder whose SMS was already dispatched; on the next run, if that reminder's count crosses 1 while it remains unscheduled-eligible, it is deleted by the new deleteMany branch, cancelling a legitimately retryable reminder while the API reports ok.

goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new OR branch in the deleteMany where clause drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so any reminder of any method with retryCount > 1 is deleted, not just SMS reminders. Email or other non-SMS workflow reminders whose retryCount exceeds 1 are hard-deleted by this handler, permanently destroying scheduled reminders for bookings before they fire — silent data loss with no recovery path (deleteMany is not soft-delete).

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` filter was changed from `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` + `scheduledDate <= now` to an `OR` of (SMS + past scheduledDate) OR (`retryCount > 1`). That second OR branch has no `method` constraint, so it will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` record with `retryCount > 1` regardless of method (email/other), which is unintended for an SMS-only handler and is irreversible since it’s a hard delete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retryCount increment uses a non-atomic read-then-write (reminder.retryCount + 1) inside a loop over stale in-memory data, and the catch-block update runs against a reminder that may have been deleted earlier in the same run. Concurrent executions of this scheduler (overlapping cron invocations) undercount retries, so failed SMS reminders are retried indefinitely — the retry cap the change exists to enforce is bypassed; the catch-path update on a deleted id throws P2025, aborting the remaining loop iterations so later reminders are never scheduled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff increments `retryCount` via a read-then-write (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) in both the non-scheduled path and the `catch` path. This is non-atomic and uses a potentially stale value from the earlier `findMany` result, so overlapping scheduler executions can clobber each other’s increments (e.g., two runs both write `1`), preventing `retryCount` from ever exceeding `1` and thus bypassing the new deletion cap (`deleteMany` deletes only `retryCount > 1`). Additionally, the `catch`-block `update({ where: { id: reminder.id }})` can throw if the row was deleted by another concurrent run (or by the initial `deleteMany` in that other run), and since that update isn’t guarded, it can abort processing of later reminders in the loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new `OR: [{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` branch in the deleteMany destroys failed reminders instead of just unscheduling them, deleting rows whose scheduledDate is still in the future. Any SMS reminder that failed to schedule twice (retryCount reaches 2) is permanently deleted from WorkflowReminder even though its scheduledDate is in the future — the booking's step loses its reminder record entirely (no cancelled flag, no audit trail), and the attendee silently never gets the SMS; this is unconditional destructive DELETE with no backup/export path, and the loss is silent because the loop below simply finds nothing to schedule.

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteMany`, the new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is not constrained by `method` or `scheduledDate`, so it will delete any `WorkflowReminder` row (including ones with `scheduledDate` still in the future, and even non-SMS methods) once `retryCount` exceeds 1. Since `retryCount` is incremented on failures (`reminder.retryCount + 1` in both the `else` and `catch` blocks), a reminder can reach 2 and then be permanently removed on the next handler run, causing loss of the reminder record/audit trail and preventing future scheduling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] retryCount is never reset to 0 on successful scheduling, so transient failures accumulate across independent scheduling cycles. A reminder that failed once months ago (retryCount=1), was scheduled successfully on the next run, and then hits a single new Twilio failure is deleted at retryCount=2 — the counter measures lifetime failures, not consecutive retries, so a single transient outage permanently destroys the reminder that the retry-count design intended to allow.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` and deletes reminders where `retryCount > 1` (deleteMany `OR` clause). `retryCount` is incremented on failure paths (both the `else` when `scheduledSMS.sid` is falsy and in `catch`), but on the success path (when `scheduledSMS.sid` exists) the update only sets `referenceId` and does not reset `retryCount` to 0. Therefore failures accumulate over time rather than representing consecutive retries, making later single failures able to trigger deletion once the lifetime count exceeds 1.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The catch-block increments retryCount via `where: { id: reminder.id }` with no guard for the record having been concurrently deleted (e.g., by the deleteMany in a parallel pod or a booking cancellation) or for the update itself failing. When the row is gone between fetch and update, Prisma throws P2025 out of the catch block, the handler returns a 500, and the remaining reminders in the loop are never processed — one dead record wedges the whole scheduling pass.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ where: { id: reminder.id }, data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } })` both in the `else` branch and inside the `catch` block. Prisma `update` throws (e.g., P2025) if the row no longer exists. Since this `update` in the `catch` is not itself guarded, a concurrent deletion (e.g., another pod running the new `deleteMany` at the top, or some other code deleting the reminder) can cause the catch-block to throw and abort the handler/loop, preventing remaining reminders from being processed. This new failure mode is introduced by the retryCount logic in the diff.

A reminder whose Twilio send failed twice (e.g., transient provider outage) is silently dropped from the database on the next cron invocation; the API still returns `{ ok: true }` and the booking recipient never receives the reminder and no one is told — silent partial success / dropped work.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the cleanup deleteMany to `where: { OR: [ { method: SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: now } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] }`, which will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1` regardless of `scheduledDate` (including future reminders) and regardless of method. The same diff increments `retryCount` on scheduling failure (both in the `else` branch and in `catch`), so a reminder that fails twice can be permanently removed on the next cron invocation with no signaling in this handler (it returns `{ ok: true }` when nothing to schedule). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Both the else-branch and the catch block increment retryCount with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` computed from the value read before the loop's awaits, instead of an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`, so concurrent invocations of the endpoint interleave and lost updates occur. If this handler runs concurrently (overlapping cron runs or a manual trigger racing the cron), two workers read the same retryCount, each write `read+1`, and one failure is counted once instead of twice — the reminder's retry budget is silently over-extended (or the deleteMany cleanup never triggers), leaving stale unscheduled reminders that neither send nor get cleaned up.
matched_golden_ids: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
